title: G76 Threading Cycle for CNC Lathes (Fanuc)

tips.title: G76 Fanuc P-word 6-digit format
tips.body: Fanuc G76 double-line format uses a 6-digit P-word on line 1: P(mm)(rr)(aa) where mm=spring passes (01-99), rr=chamfer amount (01-99), aa=tool nose angle (80,60,55,30,29,0). Example: P021029 = 2 spring passes, 10 chamfer units, 29° tool angle. A58 produces 29° infeed for 60° threads.

tips.title: G76 spring passes with G92 fallback
tips.body: If your control's G76 doesn't support spring passes natively, add G92 threading cycles immediately after G76 at the same final depth. 1-2 spring passes typically suffice. Spring passes combat part deflection (spring-back) and clean up the thread form. This works on Fanuc single-line, Haas, and older controls.

tips.title: G76 infeed angle selection: A58 vs A60
tips.body: For 60° threads, A58 produces 29° infeed (cuts mostly on one flank, light rub on other), while A60 produces 30° infeed (cuts on one flank only). A58/29° is preferred for better chip control and balanced insert wear. Radial infeed (A0) works for fine pitches but causes V-shaped chips and high temperatures on coarse threads.

tips.title: G76 first pass depth should be the deepest
tips.body: Set the first threading pass to be the deepest cut. Subsequent passes get progressively shallower due to the triangular thread cutter geometry — more area is engaged as you go deeper. The constant-area method (sqrt progression) maintains consistent chip load. Typical first pass: 0.015-0.020" for 1/4-20.

tips.title: G76 minimum cutting depth vs finish allowance
tips.body: The minimum cutting depth parameter (Fanuc Q on line 1) must be ≤ finish allowance. If min depth > finish allowance, the control may skip the finish pass entirely, leaving threads undercut. Always verify with a G-code simulator before running.

tips.title: G76 slow RPM for synchronization issues
tips.body: If threading passes aren't synchronizing properly (thread start position varies), reduce spindle RPM. Fast feedrates stress the spindle encoder synchronization. Threading feedrate = pitch, so RPM directly controls how fast you're moving. Start slower and increase only after confirming consistent thread start.

tips.title: LinuxCNC G76 depth regression parameter R
tips.body: LinuxCNC/PathPilot G76 has an R parameter for depth regression: R=1 for constant depth per pass, R=2 for constant area (chip load). R=2 is the default and preferred for most threading as it maintains consistent cutting forces. R=1 is useful for very fine threads where constant small passes are acceptable.

tips.title: G76 chamfering at thread shoulder
tips.body: Use the chamfer parameter to cleanly end threads at a shoulder. On Fanuc double-line, digits 3-4 of the P-word control chamfer (01-99 units). On Mach3, use the L parameter. Chamfering prevents sharp thread ends and improves assembly fit when threading to a shoulder.
